skill.description: Use Apple Human Interface Guidelines to design system experience components, including widgets, Live Activities, notifications, complications, quick actions, Top Shelf, App Clips, and App Shortcuts.

content.value_statement: Designing Apple system surfaces requires many platform-specific rules. This skill organizes Apple HIG guidance for widgets, Live Activities, notifications, complications, quick actions, Top Shelf, App Clips, and App Shortcuts.
actual_capabilities: Recommends the best Apple system surface for a product need.
Summarizes content strategy for widgets, Live Activities, and notifications.
Explains sizing, family, and layout guidance for system components.
Highlights update frequency and privacy constraints for glanceable experiences.
Connects App Clips, App Shortcuts, quick actions, and Top Shelf to user tasks.
limitations: It does not replace Apple developer documentation or App Review guidance.
It does not generate production Swift, SwiftUI, or ActivityKit code.
It cannot verify behavior on real devices or simulator builds.
It depends on the included reference snapshots and may not reflect later Apple changes.

use_cases.title: Select the right surface
use_cases.description: Compare widgets, Live Activities, notifications, and shortcuts for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Plan implementation scope
use_cases.description: Identify required sizes, update behavior, privacy limits, and deep-link destinations before development.

use_cases.title: Review release readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed system experience is glanceable, useful, respectful, and aligned with Apple guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a system surface
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a feature recommendation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend the best Apple system surface for my feature. Feature: [describe the feature]. Platform: [iOS, watchOS, tvOS, or macOS]. Update frequency: [how often data changes].

prompt_templates.title: Review a widget concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a planned widget.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my widget concept against Apple HIG guidance. Include content priority, supported sizes, interaction behavior, privacy concerns, and update frequency. Concept: [describe the widget].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-surface experience
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across several Apple system components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a coherent system experience across widgets, Live Activities, notifications, and App Shortcuts. Product goal: [goal]. User context: [context]. Constraints: [privacy, data, or platform limits].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a launch proposal
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness review before implementation or release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit this Apple system experience proposal. Flag HIG conflicts, weak content choices, missing variants, privacy risks, and unclear deep-link behavior. Proposal: [paste proposal].

output_examples.input: A delivery app wants status updates while an order is active.
output_examples.output: Recommend a Live Activity for active delivery tracking, with a notification only for essential changes. Use a deep link to the order detail screen.

output_examples.input: A finance app wants a Home Screen glance for selected accounts.
output_examples.output: Recommend a configurable widget with concise balances or trend summaries. Avoid sensitive details on locked or shared surfaces.

output_examples.input: A media app wants better discovery on Apple TV.
output_examples.output: Recommend Top Shelf content that highlights new or personalized media. Avoid ads, prices, and static images that imply interactivity.

best_practices: Provide the platform, user task, data freshness, and privacy constraints before asking for guidance.
Ask for surface recommendations before committing to a specific component.
Use the output as a design checklist, then verify with current Apple documentation and device testing.
anti_patterns: Do not use notifications or Live Activities for ads or low-value engagement prompts.
Do not mirror app screens directly inside widgets or other glanceable surfaces.
Do not include sensitive personal data on surfaces visible from the Lock Screen or shared environments.

faq.question: What Apple components does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers widgets, Live Activities, notifications, complications, quick actions, Top Shelf, watch faces, App Clips, and App Shortcuts.

faq.question: Can it choose between widgets and Live Activities?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare stable glanceable information with time-bound real-time tracking needs.

faq.question: Does it write production Apple platform code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and planning guidance, not production Swift or SwiftUI implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with privacy review?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights sensitive information risks on Lock Screen, watchOS, and other visible surfaces.

faq.question: Should I still read Apple documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Use this skill for structured guidance, then confirm current requirements in official Apple documentation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
